newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia eyes industry aid, tax breaks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Australia eyes industry aid, tax breaks - paper.

text.p: The Australian government would consider tax incentives to attract new industry and boost job creation in a special cabinet meeting on industry assistance on Monday, the Australian newspaper said.

Prime Minister John Howard ordered the planned cabinet agenda be postponed to look at industry aid issues, focussing on the information technology, telecoms and online industries, the paper said, without citing sources.
The paper did not detail any proposals being considered.
Government officials would not comment on the report.
The conservative Liberal-National government is under pressure over Australia's high jobless rate and is being pressed to do more to increase jobs growth.
Unemployment fell to 8.5 percent, seasonally-adjusted, in June from 8.8 percent a month earlier.
But the improvement was largely caused by people giving up looking for work, rather than an increase in employment.
The government has projected unemployment to fall to 8.25 percent, year-average, in the fiscal year which began on July 1.
